Work permit / Non-B processing times and government fees. Not researched.

name: Thailand

languages.note: English-only engineering roles exist mainly at regional tech and product companies in Bangkok. Most local listings (e.g. JobThai) are in Thai, and many require Thai.

salary.note: Levels.fyi TOTAL COMPENSATION, 25th-75th percentile, 106 data points, updated 2026-11-22. The median of THB 2.07M/yr (about THB 172,582/month) is senior-specific, but the percentiles may cover all levels. The data skews heavily to a few large Bangkok tech employers, so local-company pay is likely much lower.

income_tax_note: Progressive personal income tax; 2026 rates not verified this session. The LTR route reportedly offers a 17% flat rate for highly-skilled professionals (unverified).
cost_of_living_note: Moderate in Bangkok; no figures researched.

visa_routes.name: Non-Immigrant B visa + Work Permit (Department of Employment)

salary_threshold.note: Forum and secondary sources say there is no salary floor for the work permit itself, but nationality-tiered minimum incomes apply to the one-year extension of stay (Order 327/2557). The figure for Indian nationals is not officially confirmed (one secondary source says THB 35,000).

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Not confirmed in the material found.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: No Thai rule specific to 3-year degrees was found. Degree treatment for the work permit is unconfirmed.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: No lottery. Each work permit at a non-BOI employer reportedly needs THB 2M paid-up capital and 4 Thai employees.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Thai PR has an employment category, which is quota-based. Not researched.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Non-BOI employers: about THB 2,000,000 paid-up capital and 4 Thai employees per foreign work permit (law-firm sources). BOI-promoted companies are reportedly exempt from the ratio. Government fees not researched.

visa_routes.name: SMART Visa - T (Talent), BOI

salary_threshold.note: Minimum income of THB 100,000/month, or THB 50,000 for startup employees or retired experts (Bangkok Post). Older documents show THB 200,000, which is outdated. The employer must be in one of the targeted S-curve industries (including Digital), and the role must be endorsed by an agency in BOI's Strategic Talent Center network (e.g. the Digital Economy Promotion Agency for digital roles). Requires a Thai employment contract of at least 1 year. Work-permit exempt.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Science/technology expertise relevant to the targeted industry. A specific degree rule was not confirmed.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: The employer must be in a targeted industry and the role certified. Fees not researched.

visa_routes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Highly-Skilled Professional, BOI

salary_threshold.note: Average personal income of at least USD 80,000/year over the past 2 years. Alternative: USD 40,000/year plus a master's degree in science or technology (or IP ownership / Series A funding). The 2025 update removed the work-experience requirement. The employer must be in a targeted industry, an approved institution or a Thai government agency. Issuance fee reportedly THB 50,000. Thresholds from the BOI 2025 brochure via search results.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: None on the USD 80,000 route; a master's in science/technology on the USD 40,000 route.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: A bachelor's (3-year or 4-year) does not unlock the USD 40,000 route. The candidate needs USD 80,000+ average income, which exceeds the Thailand senior median.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: The employer must be in a qualifying industry or institution. Fees not verified.

sponsor_register.name: None found. There is no public list of work-permit-approved employers.
sponsor_register.how_to_use: Nothing to match against. Positive signals: BOI-promoted status (exempt from the 4:1 ratio; reportedly sponsors more easily) or a mention of SMART/LTR endorsement. A BOI list of promoted companies was not verified. A company record in the Thai Department of Business Development (DBD) registry is a basic legitimacy check (API not verified).

ease_for_indian_nationals.rationale: Bangkok tech hubs do hire foreign engineers, and BOI/SMART routes exist. However, non-BOI employers face per-permit capital and 4:1 Thai staffing rules, many listings require Thai, and LTR's USD 80K bar is above typical senior pay. Thailand is also the main transit point for job-scam trafficking of Indians, so every Thai offer needs heavy verification.

scam_warnings: CRITICAL: Thailand is the main transit point for trafficking Indian job-seekers into cyber-scam compounds. Embassy of India Bangkok, 19 Sep 2024: Indians are 'lured with lucrative employment offers from dubious/non-existent firms in Thailand' and then 'illegally taken across the land border' to scam centres in neighbouring countries. Recruitment runs online and offline through social media and agents, in India and overseas.

Visa-free entry to Thailand for Indians is 'meant for tourism purposes only, and it does not permit any type of employment' (Embassy of India Bangkok). Any offer to fly in visa-free or on visa-on-arrival and 'arrange the work permit later' is a scam signal. A real job needs a Non-B visa plus work permit, or a SMART/LTR endorsement, before starting work.

MEA (2022): IT-skilled youth were lured by 'data entry' and 'digital sales and marketing executive' jobs in Thailand through social media and Dubai- and India-based agents, then taken into the Myawaddy area of Myanmar to work for call-centre and crypto-fraud firms.

Named danger areas: Myawaddy and the Hpa Lu area south of Myawaddy, Myanmar (Indian Embassy Yangon, Jul 2024); Mae Sot, Thailand, the border crossing through which 549 Indians were repatriated by special flights on 10-11 Mar 2025; the Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone, Laos (May 2024 advisory: fake 'Digital Sales and Marketing Executive' and 'Customer Support Service' jobs; Lao authorities do not issue work permits to Indians entering on visa-on-arrival); Cambodia (use only MEA-authorised agents; just over 1,000 Indians rescued since 2022).

App-detectable red flags: workplace in Tak province / Mae Sot, near the Myanmar border, or the Golden Triangle; job titles like 'data entry', 'typing', 'digital marketing executive', 'customer support', 'crypto' with unusually high pay and low requirements; recruitment only through WhatsApp/Telegram/Facebook; recruiter in Dubai or India acting for a Thai 'company'; free flights or 'visa-free entry, work permit later'; interview only by chat; company not found in the Thai DBD registry or with no website; any upfront fee from the candidate.
Embassy guidance: thoroughly verify the antecedents of recruiting agents and companies, enter only on the correct visa, and never pay unauthorised persons during rescue or repatriation.
